meta.title: B2B Content Marketing | Commercial Content | CommView
meta.description: B2B content marketing with commercial purpose. Connect ICP, search demand, point of view and sales enablement through a repeatable content operation.

hero.sub: Content can help buyers discover you, understand the problem, compare approaches, trust your expertise or move a sales conversation forward. We build the content system around those jobs rather than a publishing quota.

diagram.caption: CONTENT WITH A JOB
diagram.sub: Different content should do different work.

sections.heading: A B2B Content Strategy Starts With the ICP and Buying Decision
intro: The content plan should follow what the right buyer needs to discover, understand, believe or prove at different points in the journey.
That means combining search demand, customer questions, sales evidence and a clear point of view rather than filling a calendar because the business thinks it should publish every week.

sections.heading: SEO Content, POV Content and Sales Enablement Do Different Work

items.title: SEO content
items.body: Meet relevant existing demand with useful pages built around the questions and searches buyers already make.

items.title: POV content
items.body: Give the market a reason to think differently about a problem, category or decision and make the company's judgement visible.

items.title: Sales enablement
items.body: Help a buyer or salesperson resolve questions, objections, comparisons and proof during a live commercial process.

items.title: Product and service content
items.body: Explain the offer clearly enough for the right customer to understand fit, value and the next step.

sections.heading: Content Operations Is the Machine That Keeps Useful Content Shipping
sections.intro: A strategy without a production and distribution system becomes a backlog.

steps.title: Prioritise
steps.body: Choose content from commercial need, buyer evidence and search opportunity.

steps.title: Brief
steps.body: Define the job, audience, angle, evidence and destination before drafting.

steps.title: Create
steps.body: Use subject expertise, research and AI assistance where useful without outsourcing judgement.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: Check accuracy, point of view, brand and whether the piece actually does its intended job.

steps.title: Distribute
steps.body: Put the content where the intended audience can encounter or use it.

steps.title: Measure
steps.body: Look at the behaviour and commercial signals appropriate to that content type.

items.q: How much content does a B2B scale-up actually need?
items.a: There is no useful universal publishing volume. A scale-up needs enough content to cover the important buyer questions, commercial pages, search opportunities and sales needs it has prioritised. Ten useful pieces can be more valuable than fifty generic ones. We build the roadmap from the jobs content needs to do, then set a sustainable cadence.

items.q: SEO content vs POV content: which should we invest in?
items.a: Most B2B companies need both, but they do different jobs. SEO content can capture existing search demand, while point-of-view content can create distinction and shape how the market thinks about a problem. The mix should follow your growth constraint, existing visibility, category maturity and the questions buyers need answered.

items.q: How do we measure content marketing ROI in B2B?
items.a: Measure content according to its intended job and connect it to commercial behaviour where possible. That can include non-brand discovery, target-account engagement, conversion, assisted pipeline, sales usage and influence on active opportunities. Attribution will not perfectly explain every B2B buying decision, so we combine quantitative evidence with sales and customer feedback.

sections.heading: Publishing more is not a content strategy.
sections.body: Build the content the buyer and commercial system actually need.
